Fixed the same class of bug across ~18 files: $x = if (cond) {...} else { @() } assigns $null instead of an empty array when the else branch runs, because PowerShell does not preserve 'zero output objects' as a value across an if/else used as an expression (proven: $null -eq (if ($false) { 1 } else { @() }) is True). Confirmed via Manage-LlmWikiInstructionOutcome.ps1 crashing wiki.ps1 instruction-outcome-metrics on first real (non-empty) registry data. Wrapped each affected assignment in an outer @(...) so the else branch reliably yields an empty array instead of null. Documented output shapes and behavior for non-empty branches are unchanged.
